verified_claim: NIDDK explicitly states that autoimmune thyroid injury damages the gland and reduces its ability to produce sufficient thyroid hormones. It identifies hypothyroidism as a common consequence of Hashimoto disease and explains that many affected patients develop hypothyroidism as their disease progresses.
limitation_note: The relationship is a possible progression rather than an inevitable consequence of every case of thyroid inflammation. Some patients initially retain normal thyroid function, and the article describes rare transient hyperthyroidism associated with hormone release from damaged tissue. The source does not quantify a specific damage threshold necessary for reduced hormone production.
